subject: Megacorp: measurement attribution, regional sampling, and credit calculation playbook
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@megacorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>; procure@megacorp.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: measurement windows and blackout handling

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the draft SLA language — a couple of clarifying questions from the procurement team as we prepare the SOW:

- For regional latency commitments, do you compute p95/p99 per-region, or global across all regions and then attribute back?
- How do you treat scheduled maintenance windows and announced platform upgrades? Are those excluded from measurement, and if so what notice is required?
- If only a subset of regions are impacted (e.g., us-west degraded for 3 hours), how do you calculate service credits? Is it proportional to impacted capacity, number of affected customers, or a binary outage?
- Can you share the actual queries or aggregation approach you use to compute the percentiles (we will validate against our monitoring)?

We need this detail to include in our procurement worksheet. If you can attach a short playbook / sample queries that would be great.

Best,
Alex
Alex Nguyen
Director, Cloud Procurement — MegaCorp Financial
Alex.Nguyen@megacorp.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: measurement windows and blackout handling

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise playbook and a worked example. High-level answers here, full details in the attachment (redwood_regional_sampling_playbook_v1.pdf):

- Per-region baseline: We compute p50/p90/p95/p99 per-region (region = geographic region / AZ grouping) from sampling probes and edge request latencies. We do NOT compute a global percentile and back-attribute; attribution is region-first so impacted customers in region X see credits based on region X measurements.

- Maintenance & announced upgrades: Scheduled maintenance windows that we announce at least 48 hours in advance are excluded from measurement. Emergency maintenance is handled case-by-case and documented in incident notes; we exclude only if we post the maintenance notice with a start/end window and it meets the emergency maintenance criteria in section 3.2 of the playbook.

- Partial/regional impact credits: Credits are proportional to impacted capacity-weighted duration. Practically: we compute the fraction of traffic (or healthy serving capacity) degraded in the region during the interval and prorate credits by (affected_capacity_fraction) * (duration_fraction) * (SLA weight). Example calculations are in the attached workbook.

- Queries / aggregation: Included (sample_aggregation_sql.sql) — we provide the exact SQL we run against our telemetry warehouse to reproduce p95/p99 and affected_capacity metrics. Note: queries reference the telemetry_map.csv for metric names and mapping.

Next steps: Karthik and Laura will add the precise formulas and example outputs (CSV) to the playbook; happy to run a short 2-week validation pilot against your monitoring if you want to ground-truth numbers.

Jordan

Adding the telemetry/aggregation details Alex asked for. I pulled the core math into a short note and attached a sample SQL extract. Key points:

1) Sampling and aggregation windows
- We compute per-region percentiles on 5-minute buckets; rolling 5-minute windows are aggregated into hourly summaries to avoid excessive noise from transient spikes.
- P95/P99 are calculated from request-level latency histograms collected at edge proxy and normalized by request size class.

2) Capacity / impact fraction definition (for partial outages)
- affected_capacity_fraction = sum(egress_capacity_of_impacted_nodes) / sum(total_egress_capacity_in_region) measured at minute resolution.
- credit_fraction_for_interval = affected_capacity_fraction * (interval_duration_minutes/total_SLA_window_minutes).

3) Credit application examples
- If us-west loses 30% of egress capacity for 3 hours within a 30-day SLA window, the proration is 0.30 * (3*60)/(30*24*60) = 0.30 * 0.00417 = 0.00125 -> credit equals SLA_level * 0.125% of monthly fee (worked examples attached).

4) Telemetry sources and reconciliation
- Primary: edge-proxy request traces (latency histograms), sampling probes, and request routing logs.
- Reconciliation uses unique request IDs and a join on minute timestamps; we drop probe samples during maintenance windows.

I've attached sample_aggregation_sql.sql and telemetry_map.csv that map our metric names and the key joins. These are intended for tooling validation by your SREs.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

Jordan / Karthik — this is helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from procurement and our SRE reviewer:

- How do you treat traffic throttling due to quota constraints vs. actual service degradation? Our concern is credits being triggered by client-side throttling or rate-limit configuration differences.
- Caching layers: if an edge cache returns stale content faster, how is that accounted for in p95 (since it artificially lowers latency for some customers)?
- Emergency maintenance: can you propose wording we can use that limits exclusions to planned/emergency windows where Redwood initiates or coordinates the action? We want to avoid overly broad "customer-driven" exclusions.

Also: please drop the HubSpot deal link in the thread so procurement can tie this to the SOW. We'll also need an example monthly report we can consume automatically (CSV export).

Best,

Subject: Re: Clarification: measurement windows and blackout handling — consolidated playbook and next steps

Alex — thanks for the questions, and appreciate the detail from your SRE reviewer. We've consolidated everything into version 2 of the measurement playbook and a short calculation workbook (attached). Highlights and our proposed contractual language you can drop into the SOW: 

- Quota/throttling: We differentiate throttling caused by client-side rate limits vs. server-side throttling. Only server-side (Redwood-controlled) throttling that causes inability to serve valid requests is eligible for credit. We instrument both sides and tie credits to server-side metrics (see section 4.1 of the playbook).

- Caching: Edge cache hits are annotated and excluded from latency percentiles used for SLA calculations where the cached response materially affects user-observed latency (see cache policy table). For endpoints where caching is expected, we offer a caching-aware SLA variant; details in the workbook.

- Emergency maintenance wording (proposed): 
  "Emergency maintenance": unscheduled activity initiated by Redwood to mitigate an active or imminent threat to service integrity. Emergency maintenance windows are eligible for exclusion only when Redwood posts an incident notice with start/end timestamps and a concise justification signed by the on-call service owner.

- Automation & reporting: We can provide a CSV export of monthly measurement results (per-region p50/p90/p95/p99, downtime minutes, credit calculations) delivered to a secure S3/SharePoint location. Example CSV format attached.

Proposed next steps:
1) 2-week measurement validation pilot (Redwood runs our queries in parallel with your SREs) — start window: within 7 business days after SOW signature.
2) Deliver monthly automated CSV and a quarterly reconciliation meeting.
3) Contract clause: include the capacity-weighted proration formula in the SLA exhibit and reference the playbook for operational definitions.

If that aligns, we'll update the SOW language and send a redline for your legal/procurement review. Attaching: redwood_sla_measurement_playbook_v2.pdf, calculation_examples.xlsx.

Thanks,
Jordan
